name: film-crew
description: A film crew for making videos. Give the director a topic and a style and it runs the whole production: a screenwriter researches it and writes a script where every spoken fact carries two sources, a story editor engineers the hooks and open loops, a voice booth narrates it, a storyboard artist plans a visual beat every few seconds, an animation director budgets the motion the way a TV anime budgets drawings — most beats held nearly still so one or two can have everything — and a production designer shoots it in a chosen style: archival paper collage, mid-century flat vector, or a broadcast news bulletin, with more added as folders. Paper and flat share a compiler, so the same storyboard renders in either look and a film's style can be chosen by watching both. Each shot is staged as a scene rather than a lone cutout, journeys are shown as movement, backgrounds are held per act the way limited animation does, the camera pans between scenes instead of cutting, and the palette, score, ambience and sound effects are all chosen from the story rather than from a default — the score spotted into cues per act rather than one loop wall to wall. Cuts vertical Shorts from the hookiest moments, packages everything for YouTube, and publishes only what a human has approved. Also assembles long recorded sessions into episodes and Shorts.
